value.rationale: Even bipyramids are canonical simplicial convex-polytope one-skeletons with a natural increasing rim parameter and closed-form perfect-matching enumeration. Classifying the first three nontrivial sizes after the octahedral base case exposes a sharp qualitative transition: the six- and eight-rim complexes have homology in one degree while the ten-rim complex has free integral homology in adjacent dimensions two and three. An exact finite threshold and its sphere-wedge description provide a meaningful, reusable test family for general perfect-matching-complex topology, not merely a Betti-table recomputation.
